hints: Notice the three numbers in the stem: wavelength $\lambda = 500\text{ nm}$, fringe spacing $x = 5\text{ mm}$, and the paired $D$ and $a$ values in the table.
Recall the double-slit fringe spacing relation $x = \lambda D / a$, so the observed $x$ fixes the ratio $D/a$.
Convert $x$ and $\lambda$ to metres, calculate $x/\lambda$, then check which $D$ in metres divided by $a$ in metres gives that same value.
walkthrough: Write the givens in SI units: $\lambda = 500\text{ nm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}$ and fringe spacing $x = 5\text{ mm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$.
State the governing rule for two-source interference: fringe spacing $x = \lambda D / a$, where $D$ is slit-screen distance and $a$ is slit separation.
Rearrange to isolate the ratio set by the observation: $D/a = x/\lambda$.

Test the table values: only $D = 5\text{ m}$ with $a = 0.5\text{ mm} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$ gives $D/a = 5/(5.0 \times 10^{-4}) = 1.0 \times 10^{4}$, matching the required ratio and giving $x = 5\text{ mm}$.

options.A: With $D = 0.50\text{ m}$ and $a = 0.5\text{ mm}$ the ratio $D/a = 1000$, which gives $x = 0.5\text{ mm}$, ten times too small.
options.B: With $D = 0.50\text{ m}$ and $a = 5\text{ mm}$ the ratio $D/a = 100$, which gives $x = 0.05\text{ mm}$, far smaller than $5\text{ mm}$.
options.C: With $D = 5\text{ m}$ and $a = 0.5\text{ mm}$ the ratio $D/a = 10000$, which gives $x = 5\text{ mm}$ for $\lambda = 500\text{ nm}$.
options.D: With $D = 5\text{ m}$ and $a = 5\text{ mm}$ the ratio $D/a = 1000$, which gives $x = 0.5\text{ mm}$, ten times too small.
